signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Repricing
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades down to 188.58 as JPY gains an average of +1.198% across 7 pairs while CHF sheds −0.733% across 6 pairs over the trailing week, generating a 1.931% G10 leader-to-laggard divergence. The policy rate differential of SNB 0.00% vs BoJ 1.25% gives JPY a 125bp carry advantage over CHF, while the 25d risk reversals show a pronounced EUR/JPY put skew at −2.63 and USD/JPY at −2.61, signaling substantial options demand for downside yen-cross protection. In CFTC positioning, JPY leveraged funds net long stands at +4,472 (52-week percentile 98, z +2.66), reflecting extreme institutional positioning despite a WoW liquidation of −15,597 contracts, whereas CHF spec net short sits in the lower decile at −18,620 (52-week percentile 2, z −2.30). Cross-asset bond volatility remains elevated with the MOVE index at 106.6 (98th percentile of its trailing year) against a quiescent VIX at 16.0 (27th percentile), reflecting bond-market pricing of policy divergence that equity volatility has yet to register. Spot CHF/JPY now trades well below its BEER fair-value estimate of 195.84 (model z −1.92σ), underscoring the structural pressure on the cross. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY; policy rate spread and G10 divergence favor continued JPY outperformance. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions and Tankan survey due at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot recovery and daily close above 190.50 invalidate the near-term downside structure.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry Tension
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.28, holding between its rising 20-day SMA at 156.28 and resistance at the 50-day and 200-day SMA cluster near 158.49/158.45. The cash overnight spread of SOFR 3.90% vs TONA 1.23% preserves a 267bp carry advantage that structurally underpins the base currency. However, 1-month 25-delta risk reversals exhibit an acute downside put skew of −2.61, demonstrating heavy demand for downside strike protection against potential official pushback near recent highs. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds holding +4,472 net long JPY contracts at the 98th percentile of their 52-week range (z +2.66), even as speculative accounts trimmed −15,597 contracts WoW. Simultaneously, 1-month implied volatility sits at 9.2% versus realized 30-day volatility of 10.1%, printing a negative vol risk premium of −1.0% that highlights options mispricing relative to historical movement. Trade bias: Range-bound USD/JPY; carry advantage competes against persistent options market hedging. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions and Tankan release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Sustained break above the 158.50 moving average barrier forces downside hedge unwinds.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Compression Ahead of Asia Event Risk
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6990, slipping below its 20-day SMA (0.7134), 50-day SMA (0.7096), and 200-day SMA (0.7028) to enter an intraday technical breakdown posture. Cash yields show RBA cash rate at 4.60% vs Fed funds at 4.00%, offering a nominal 60bp carry advantage in favor of AUD (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.90% gives a 45bp net carry advantage). CFTC leveraged funds hold a net long position of +55,684 contracts (74.5% long, 52-week percentile 81, z +0.92), although net length stalled with a WoW reduction of −3,615 contracts as price action deteriorated. That institutional length contrasts with retail positioning, where retail accounts remain 77% net long, leaving positioning one-sided. Australian data remains solid with domestic ESI at +11.0, but markets confront imminent Asian macro catalysts spanning Australian CPI and Chinese manufacturing PMIs. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish AUD/USD; technical loss of the 200-day SMA at 0.7028 weighs against carry support. Catalyst: Australia August CPI indicator previewed at 4.0% along with China official PMIs during the Asia session. Risk: An upside CPI print above 4.2% sparks an institutional short squeeze back through 0.7030.
evidence: RBA 4.6% vs Fed 4.0% — -60bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: USD/CAD — Positioning Divergence + Crude Breakdown
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4189, extending gains above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day SMA cluster situated between 1.3844 and 1.3949. Front-end monetary divergence remains stark with Fed policy at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.25%, producing a 175bp nominal carry spread (SOFR 3.90% vs CORRA 2.30% provides a +160bp carry advantage to the US dollar). CFTC leveraged funds carry a substantial net short CAD exposure of −49,123 contracts (52-week percentile 69, z +0.69) with net selling accelerating by −7,719 contracts WoW. This speculative bearishness directly diverges from Retail sentiment data retail sentiment, where retail accounts are positioned 94% net short the pair (only 6% long), establishing an acute positioning imbalance. Downside pressure on the Canadian dollar is amplified by a 4.04% intraday slide in WTI crude oil prices to $88.90 per barrel, eroding terms-of-trade backing for CAD. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; rate spread and energy price decline reinforce trend continuation over contrarian retail positioning. Catalyst: US ADP employment and Core PCE releases at 12:15-12:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp crude oil rebound above $92.00 triggers immediate profit-taking on institutional CAD shorts.
